title: Chandler Reclaimed Water Operating System — Phase 65 Agriculture and bioeconomy review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Agriculture and bioeconomy reporting pack. Chandler describes an operating reclaimed-water network that treats roughly 11 billion gallons annually and serves industrial, irrigation, recharge, and other uses.
key_findings: The system includes three reclamation facilities and 93 miles of reclaimed-water distribution pipes.
The City reports roughly 11 billion gallons treated each year.
Avoided drinking-water demand is reported systemwide, not by industrial customer.
why_it_matters: Which records connect research and authorization to field adoption, production, resilience, water exposure, and comparable crop outcomes? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. It supplies an operating municipal comparator for the agreement-to-reuse pathway.
ftfn_relevance: Advances one named Phase 55Y reader journey.
Separates the current evidence stage from downstream operation or outcome claims.
Creates a specific next-record watch point.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The figures do not disclose individual industrial customer flows.
Systemwide volume is not evidence of spare capacity or TSMC service.
